I am beyond disappointed with my experience at Town & Country Animal Hospital. From the front desk interaction to the way the medical care was handled, the entire experience felt unprofessional and completely lacking in basic human decency and compassion.

We were taken into a room and initially spoke with a NURSE, not the attending doctor. We were repeatedly told, “Here’s what the doctor recommends,” despite never having actually spoken to the doctor. I politely asked to speak directly with the doctor because I was being asked to pay $793 and, as a pet parent, I wanted to understand the doctor’s thought process, what they were seeing, and what the next steps would be once the results came back. I don’t think that is an unreasonable request.

When the doctor finally came in, her attitude was extremely dismissive. The facial expressions and snarky remarks made me feel like my questions were somehow an inconvenience. My dog is the patient, and I am her advocate. I have every right to ask questions and understand what is happening with her care. Asking questions should never make a pet owner feel belittled.

Regardless, I still paid the $793 for a urinalysis, bloodwork, and imaging. We waited well over an hour for everything to come back. We were then placed back into a room where the doctor showed us the imaging and said she did not see any bladder stones. She told us my dog had a UTI and referred us to another emergency hospital because she believed my dog needed further imaging.

At that point, I felt like I had just paid $793 and gotten nowhere.

We went to MVS, and the experience was completely different. They immediately requested the imaging and lab work from Town & Country. The doctor came directly to speak with me, reviewed everything, and asked, “If the other hospital saw that she had a UTI, did they give you medication?” I told him NO. He literally said, “Wow.”

He then showed me the SAME imaging that Town & Country had taken and pointed out that you could clearly see the bladder stone obstructing her urinary passage.

That is extremely concerning.

I understand that mistakes can happen in medicine, but what bothered me most was the lack of communication, compassion, professionalism, and willingness to listen. When someone’s pet is sick and they are scared, the LAST thing they need is to feel like they’re being treated like an inconvenience.

I would strongly encourage other pet owners to get a second opinion and ask questions if something doesn’t feel right. Your pet cannot advocate for themselves, so you have to do it for them.
